geology_info.concentration_process: Northern Part Of District Characterized By Low- To Intermediate-Temperature Hydrothermal Formation Of Quartz Veins Relatively High Sulfide Content (Pb, Zn, Cu, Ag, And A Little Au) And Some Au-Ag Tellurides. Southern Part Characterized By Low-Temperature Hydrothermal Formation Of Quartz-Rhodochrosite-Fluorite Veins With Minor Sulfide Content But High Ag. Secondary Enrichment Was Shallow And Important In Early Production. Oxidation Of Rhodochrosite Veins In Southern Area Resulted In Formation Of Mn Ores And Moderate Ag Enrichment.

geology_info.alteration: The Volcanic Rocks Exhibit Regional Propylitic Alteration Overprinted By Silicification, And Local Potassium Flooding Or Secondary Growth On Primary Feldspars (Randolph And Ellis, 1989). Trace Amonts Of Adularia Has Been Identified As Fracture Coatings.  No Argillic Alteration Has Been Recognized.  Some Pyrite-Filled Fractures Show Narrow Kaolinite-Epidote-Sericite Alteration Envelopes. Quartz Veins May Be Accompanied By Pyritization And Silicification In The Surrounding Wall Rock.

The Silurian Host Rock Adjacent To Both The Radioactive Carbonate And The Ree-Carbonate Veins Are Commonly Marked By Alteration Zones A Few Inches Thick Adjacent To Them Marked By Dark Red By Hematititc Alteration.  The Alteration Is Somewhat More Intense Adjacent To The Radioactive Veins.
